judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper (`{success, data}`), and this call site stores that wrapper directly as the credential `key` (the replaced code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`'s data), corrupting the credential shape on every refresh. After the first token refresh, `credential.key` becomes `{success: true, data: {...}}`; the next GoogleCalendarService instantiation reads `credential.key.access_token` as undefined and Google Calendar auth fails — for all deployments, independent of whether the sync feature is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (a `SafeParseReturnType` with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This will store the wrapper object as `credential.key`, unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` which stored only the credential shape. Since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the wrapper regardless of whether sync is enabled (it uses `schema.safeParse(...)` when sync is off), this would corrupt the stored credential structure after a refresh and break later reads expecting `credential.key.access_token`.
